title: People Ops — Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Playbook
author: Ava Chen
summary: Canonical Redwood Inference People Ops playbook covering hiring processes, candidate screening, offer and acceptance workflow, employee onboarding checklist, 30-60-90 planning, performance and feedback cycles, manager responsibilities, and links to related policies.
purpose: Provide a single, actionable reference for hiring managers and people ops partners to run predictable, compliant, and high-quality hiring and onboarding experiences, and to run consistent performance and feedback cycles across teams.
scope: Applies to all full-time and fixed-term hires at Redwood Inference and to managers responsible for new hire onboarding, performance reviews, promotions, and compensation recommendations. For contractor or vendor-specific processes see the Staffing & Contractors page.
principles:
- Candidate experience is a product: fast, respectful, transparent.
- Decisions are evidence-based: use rubrics and calibrated interviews.
- Managers own team outcomes: hiring, onboarding, and performance.
- People Ops partners for policy, compliance, and compensation calibration.
- Documented, repeatable processes reduce bias and risk.
hiring_process_overview:
1) Requisition & approval: manager opens req in Greenhouse and secures hiring budget approval via finance.
2) Sourcing & screening: recruiters screen and surface diverse candidate slates.
3) Interviews & evaluation: use panel interviews + standardized rubrics.
4) Decision & compensation: hiring manager recommends, People Ops approves.
5) Offer & close: recruiter extends offer and coordinates background checks.
6) Onboarding: People Ops + manager run the 30/60/90 plan and checklist.
requisition_and_approval_steps:
1. Manager creates a draft JD using the Job Description template and submits to People Ops.
2. People Ops confirms role band, comp range, and headcount code.
3. Manager obtains budget owner sign-off (email or ticket).
4. Recruiter opens the req in Greenhouse and posts to approved channels.
5. People Ops logs the req for EEO reporting.
candidate_screening_and_sourcing_guidanc:
- Recruiter screens for minimum qualifications and role fit; a short 20-minute screen call should surface enthusiasm and baseline competence.
- Aim for at least 3 diverse, qualified candidates before opening onsite interviews.
- Use structured screening questions and take notes in Greenhouse.
- For technical roles include a take-home or paired exercise only where necessary; prefer 45–60-minute live technical interviews for time-to-offer improvements.
interview_structure_and_rubric:
Interview panel should evaluate: role competence, problem solving, communication, collaboration, and alignment with company values.
Use the standardized rubric:
- 1 = Below expectations; 2 = Needs development; 3 = Meets expectations; 4 = Exceeds expectations; 5 = Exceptional.
Each interviewer submits scores and 2–3 examples of observed behavior.
Calibration runs quarterly: People Ops will run calibration sessions to align scoring across teams.
decision_and_offer_process:
- Hiring manager completes the hire recommendation form in Greenhouse summarizing top candidate and rationale.
- People Ops performs offer feasibility check (band, comp, equity, sign-on budget).
- Recruiter prepares offer letter template with role, base, equity, bonus (if applicable), start date, and contingency conditions.
- Manager and recruiter obtain final approval from People Ops and finance.
- Offer is extended verbally and followed by a written offer within 24 hours.
- Typical negotiation window: 3 business days. For time-sensitive roles escalate to People Ops lead.
background_checks_and_eligibility:
Background checks are required for all hires in regulated roles and recommended for ICs interacting with customer data.
Process: candidate signs authorization — People Ops orders checks — vendor delivers report — People Ops reviews results and recommends next steps.
Adverse results: People Ops consults Legal and the Hiring Manager before making final decisions.
onboarding_overview: Onboarding is a shared responsibility: People Ops owns the program logistics and compliance, the manager owns role ramp and context, and the buddy/peer provides day-to-day guidance. Onboarding is at minimum a 90-day plan with explicit milestones.
onboarding_checklist: Pre-Day (1–7 days before start): complete offer paperwork, add to HRIS, send welcome email with first-day schedule and logistics, set up equipment order (IT).
Day 1: People Ops orientation (benefits, payroll, security training), manager 1:1 for role context and expectations, team welcome.
Week 1: Role-specific training, access to documentation, buddy pairing, calendar time for focused work and onboarding check-ins.
Week 2–4: Shadowing, first mini-project assigned, initial 1:1 weekly cadence established.
Month 1: 30-day check-in (manager + People Ops) to review ramp progress, blockers, and training plan.
Month 2: 60-day check-in focused on impact, autonomy, and cross-team connections.
Month 3: 90-day review: formal manager assessment, feedback exchange, and plan for next quarter.
30_60_90_template:
Suggested template for managers to share with new hires:
- 30 days (Learn): meet key partners, complete required trainings, deliver first small task.
- 60 days (Contribute): take ownership of a recurring task, present a short readout to team.
- 90 days (Impact): independently drive feature or a measurable improvement and propose next-quarter goals.
Managers should document success criteria for each milestone in the new hire's onboarding doc in Confluence.
manager_responsibilities_for_onboarding:
- Prepare role-specific onboarding docs and a first project before the hire starts.
- Schedule recurring 1:1s and weekly check-ins for the first 90 days.
- Assign a peer buddy and ensure cross-team intro meetings are scheduled.
- Provide timely feedback and escalate onboarding blockers to People Ops.
- Complete 30/60/90 written check-ins and share with People Ops.
performance_cycle_overview:
- Cadence: Continuous feedback, quarterly check-ins, and an annual formal performance review.
- Objectives: Managers and ICs set clear OKRs or goals every quarter; People Ops provides templates and timing.
- Ratings: Use the company rating scale and calibration process. Compensation cycles are aligned with performance cycles (annual review in Q1).
feedback_and_coaching_guidance:
- Encourage a culture of frequent, specific feedback (real-time + scheduled).
- Managers must document developmental feedback in the performance system and meet with direct reports at least monthly.
- When delivering corrective feedback follow the Observe + Impact + Next Steps model and document follow-up actions.
- For performance concerns start an informal coaching plan; if insufficient improvement, follow the Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) template in People Ops resources.
promotion_and_compensation_review_proces:
- Promotions are manager-nominated and require a justification memo that maps accomplishments to the promotion rubric.
- People Ops coordinates calibration meetings across functions to ensure parity.
- Compensation changes require business rationale and budget approval; total comp must fit within approved band.
- Typical timeline from nomination to effectivity: 4–8 weeks depending on calibration and approvals.
manager_guidelines_and_best_practices:
- Hire for mission and culture fit as well as capability.
- Run structured interviews and document evidence.
- Share clear goals and success metrics.
- Give regular, balanced feedback and recognize wins publicly.
- Build development plans with 1:1s focused on growth and career conversations.
- Use People Ops as a partner for escalations and policy questions.
escalation_and_risk_guidance:
- If a hiring or onboarding issue arises (offer pull, unexpected legal eligibility, failed background check), escalate to People Ops, Legal, and the hiring manager immediately.
- For performance-related legal risk (e.g., protected-class concerns) stop any adverse action and consult People Ops + Legal.
- Data privacy: new hires with access to customer data must complete Security & Data Handling training on day 1.
tools_and_templates: Canonical templates (stored in the People Ops folder): Job Description template, Interview Rubric (by function), Offer Letter templates, 30/60/90 template, Onboarding checklist, PIP template, Promotion justification memo. Use Greenhouse for tracking and Workday for HR records.
metrics_and_reporting: People Ops tracks: time-to-offer, time-to-hire, acceptance rate, source quality, new-hire retention at 3/6/12 months, 30/60/90 completion rates, and manager NPS for onboarding. Quarterly reports are published to the People Ops dashboard.
privacy_and_compliance_notes:
- All applicant data is retained per the Data Retention Policy; access is limited to recruiting and People Ops staff.
- For roles with export-controlled or regulated data, ensure the candidate's location and eligibility are validated prior to offer.
- Maintain EEO/OFCCP compliance for US hiring and equivalent local laws for other regions.
version_history: v1.0 (2023-06-01) — initial playbook; v1.4 (2024-08-10) — updated offer and background-check process; v2.0 (2026-02-15) — revised onboarding cadence and performance calibration guidance.
notes_for_managers:
- Use this playbook as the canonical source and link to the role-specific onboarding page you publish for each new hire.
- Reach out to People Ops at people-ops@redwood.ai for exceptions or urgent approvals.
- Keep onboarding docs in the team Confluence space for discoverability.
